reply_text:
I found one candidate for 2016, and it's a weak one. In a private email on 19 February 2016, Sutskever predicted a "conventionally significant result" from OpenAI within 6 to 9 months. It has a time span, but it's a forecast about his own lab's research output, not about what AI will be able to do. Read it as borderline. I found no dated forecast of when AGI would arrive.

**The candidate.** The email came out through the Musk v. Altman lawsuit, and I read it on OpenAI's own published page. He was replying to Musk, who had asked for "something significant in the next 6 to 9 months." In the same email he wrote that solving one problem would not be enough for "full human level AI." He said other problems, such as unsupervised learning, transfer learning and lifetime learning, could "see significant progress in the coming years." That has no date and isn't about when AGI arrives, so it isn't listed separately.

**Other 2016 items I checked and left out:**
- **OpenAI technical goals (20 June 2016).** He co-wrote this blog post with Brockman, Altman and Musk. It names goals such as a household robot, an agent that understands language, and one agent that solves many games, but gives no dates.
- **Email of 2 January 2016.** He wrote, "As we get closer to building AI, it will make sense to start being less open." It has no date or time span, and it isn't a statement about when AGI arrives.
- **"Next 5 years" Q&A.** His answer predicted much deeper models, learning from fewer examples, progress in unsupervised learning, and better speech and image recognition. But the RE•WORK page I opened was published on 29 December 2015, so it belongs to 2015. The LinkedIn version of the Q&A wouldn't open.

**Gaps.** I didn't find a transcript for his January 2016 RE•WORK talk or his NIPS 2016 talk, so neither was checked. All 12 searches and 6 page openings are used up. The first search ran only once: the script crashed while printing the results, but the results were kept and read. Most results were coverage of his 2024–2025 remarks, such as the "5 to 20 years" estimate.
